content: The metabolism of omeprazole is influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administering drugs that interact with this pathway. Omeprazole reduces the levels or effects of riociguat by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sparsentan reduces the levels or effects of omeprazole by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sparsentan, as a CYP2C19 inducer, decreases the exposure of CYP2C19 substrates, potentially reducing their efficacy. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Stiripentol affects omeprazole metabolism via hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Stiripentol acts as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, necessitating monitoring of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates for altered effects. Stiripentol also increases omeprazole levels by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP2C19 substrates may be required if adverse reactions occur. Omeprazole increases tacrolimus levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, especially in intermediate or poor CYP2C19 metabolizers, as tacrolimus whole blood concentrations may rise. Tazemetostat decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while omeprazole increases tazemetostat levels via the same pathway. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Omeprazole increases tinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole increases tofacitinib levels by influencing CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. No specific dose adjustment is required when tofacitinib is co-administered with potent CYP2C19 inhibitors, but dose reduction is advised if combined with moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Triclabendazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole decreases vismodegib levels by altering its solubility through increased gastric pH, potentially reducing bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Voriconazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting both CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole increases warfarin levels by influencing the metabolism of its less potent R-enantiomer, which involves CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19. Frequent INR monitoring and warfarin dose adjustments may be necessary. Acetazolamide increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases alprazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases ambrisentan levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Anastrozole increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole decreases cyanocobalamin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Cyclophosphamide increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Danazol increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Darifenacin decreases omeprazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Devil’s claw reduces omeprazole effects via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This is a theoretical interaction with unknown clinical significance. Dexamethasone decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Dronedarone increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Drospirenone increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF affects omeprazole metabolism via CYP3A4. Based on studies, no clinically significant interactions are expected with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs). Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases omeprazole effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor for gastrointestinal symptoms, as the net effect on PPI action is unclear due to opposing CYP450 actions. Omeprazole increases estazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases etravirine levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole decreases ferric carboxymaltose levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Fluoxetine increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases flurazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases glipizide levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Larotrectinib increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Levoketoconazole increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole decreases levothyroxine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Omeprazole decreases liothyronine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Omeprazole decreases liotrix levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Omeprazole reduces the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine due to reduced gastric acidity caused by PPIs. The area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. Monitor closely. Omeprazole decreases methamphetamine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor patients for changes in clinical effects and adjust therapy as needed. Omeprazole increases midazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Mitotane decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4. Monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Omeprazole increases ospemifene levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole decreases phytoestrogen levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases quazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Ribociclib increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases ruxolitinib topical levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases the toxicity of theophylline through an unspecified mechanism. Prolonged PPI use can cause hypochlorhydria, altering intestinal peristalsis. Monitor for toxicity. Omeprazole decreases thyroid desiccated levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. Omeprazole increases triazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Omeprazole increases voriconazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Monitor closely. Omeprazole increases abrocitinib levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Start abrocitinib at 50 mg daily when co-administered with CYP2C19 inhibitors. If no adequate response is achieved after 12 weeks, the dose may be increased to 100 mg daily. Omeprazole decreases acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases with increasing gastric pH. Due to the long-lasting effect of PPIs, separating doses may not eliminate the interaction. Apalutamide decreases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide is a strong inducer of these enzymes, potentially reducing the exposure and efficacy of CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 substrates. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary, and adjust doses accordingly. Armodafinil increases omeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. If co-administered, the PPI dose should not exceed a dose comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and must be taken approximately 12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients.
